subject: english-literature
title: Postcolonial and Psychoanalytic Readings
welcome_lead: Said, Spivak, Bhabha and Freud open further interpretive paths. Postcolonial and psychoanalytic lenses uncover empire and unconscious in the text.
meta_desc: English Literature: postcolonial theory (Said, Spivak, Bhabha) and psychoanalytic criticism.
final_note: Texts carry empires and unconsciouses — bring them to light.

concepts.def: Edward Said's critique of Western representations of the East as exotic Other.
Gayatri Spivak's term for those denied a voice within hegemonic discourse.
Homi Bhabha's concept of cultural mixing in colonial encounter.
Reading texts through Freudian or Lacanian frames of desire and unconscious.
Freud's das Unheimliche — the strangely familiar that disturbs.
Bhabha's term for the colonised subject's partial imitation of the coloniser.

walkthroughs.body_html: Said shows how Western texts construct the East as static and feminine. Apply the lens to A Passage to India — Forster both critiques and reproduces Orientalist tropes.
Spivak's question challenges the assumption that critics can ventriloquise oppressed voices. Even sympathetic representation may erase difference.
The uncanny is the strangely familiar — doubles, dolls, doppelgangers. Apply it to gothic fiction or Henry James's The Turn of the Screw.
